titulo: Futuro perfecto and probability: Forming the futuro perfecto

aula.objetivo: Form the futuro perfecto («habré terminado») to say what will already be finished by a future moment, and use it together with the simple future to make guesses about the present and the recent past («habrá llegado ya»).

itens.pt: at the end of the month

blocos.titulo: Habré + participle: what will have happened
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: picture a future date, say Friday. In English: "By Friday I will have finished the report." That "will have finished" is the futuro perfecto. STEP 2: Spanish builds it with the simple future of «haber» + participle: «habré terminado». English "will have" = «habré», in one word. STEP 3: the future of «haber»: habré, habrás, habrá, habremos, habréis, habrán. Four of them have an accent (habré, habrás, habrá, habréis); «habremos» doesn't. STEP 4: the participle is the usual one (hablado, comido, vivido; hecho, dicho, visto, puesto, escrito, abierto, vuelto…) and it NEVER agrees with the subject. STEP 5: use the futuro perfecto to say an action will be finished before a future moment. The typical markers are «para + time» — English "BY Friday" is «PARA el viernes», «para entonces» (by then) — and «antes de + time» («antes de las ocho»). Careful: "by" here is never «por». STEP 6: compare: «terminaré el informe» (I'll finish the report, some time) and «habré terminado el informe para el viernes» (by Friday it will be done). STEP 7: negation and pronouns go before the auxiliary: «No habré terminado», «Lo habré terminado» (I will have finished it). STEP 8: in everyday conversation, for concrete plans, many people prefer the present («para el viernes lo tengo listo» = I'll have it ready by Friday). The futuro perfecto for plans is more common in writing and formal situations; its most frequent use is guessing, which you'll see in the next session.
blocos.comparacao: English has the same tense: "will have + past participle" = «habré + participio». "I will have done" = «habré hecho». The trap is the preposition: English "BY Friday" is «PARA el viernes» (or «antes del viernes»), never «por el viernes».

tabela.exemplo: By eight you'll already have arrived.
By then we'll have done it.
By Monday you'll have come back.

erros.motivo: The future of «haber» has an accent: habré, habrás, habrá, habréis.

erros.errado: Para el viernes habré terminar el informe.
erros.certo: Para el viernes habré terminado el informe.
erros.motivo: After «haber» comes the participle, not the infinitive.
The auxiliary and the participle stay together, in that order.

blocos.enunciado: Say five sentences about what you will have done by the end of next week: «Para el viernes habré terminado… Para el domingo habré leído…»
Say out loud the simple future of hablar, comer and vivir in the first and third person («hablaré, hablará…»). Then say five participles, including an irregular one.
